title: Chapter 1024
paragraphs: Chapter 1024
Episode 247. Liberation War of Lafrarosa (12)
Lokia attempted to fire again, but the separated main cannon of Kri didn't budge. The lightning energy had completely disrupted its control.
[Oh, you're smart. Caught me off guard there.]

The cannon, dispersing into particles, began to be reabsorbed into the main body. Soon after, the warrior kings charged at Lokia, but their strikes hit nothing but air. Lokia had already transformed into a shadow, heading towards Kri.
"Huh, strange? I thought the sword had hit."
"I saw it hit too, Beliz brother."
"What's going on?"
To the Battle Kings, Lokia didn't seem too fast. In fact, his movements appeared sluggish and heavy, nothing like what one would expect from a former Ten Knight of Runcandel a thousand years ago.
[It's magic. He's used magic to disrupt your senses. I remember now. We used to call it Lokia-style magic.]
The magic of Lokia, which had saved Temar and his companions from crises a thousand years ago, was now threatening Jin and his allies.
[Get out of there immediately and come near me, Battle Kings. Unless you want to accidentally stab each other due to your disrupted senses.]
Whoosh!
Murakan gently exhaled towards the Battle Kings. Instead of the destructive energy usually used to tear apart enemies, it was a breath to help the Battle Kings not lose their way in Lokia's magic.
As the spiritual energy reached the Battle Kings, the physical manifestation of the magic became visible to them. Complex lines of magic, like tangled threads, filled the area around them.
[Don't touch those lines and carefully escape. This magic can flip the senses of even guys like you in an instant.]
The Battle Kings instinctively felt the danger upon seeing the lines of magic themselves.
lightning energy and destructive swordsmanship alone seemed insufficient to easily dismantle this peculiar magic.

[Yeah, it's been a really long time since I've fought directly. Even when I was one of the Ten Knights, I didn't enjoy roaming the battlefield. There are many ways to defeat an opponent without physically clashing. Such methods are preferred by brutish ones like Sarah.]
" Pretending to be familiar with Knight Sarah, I see."
[She's a cute one. You might be surprised, but Sarah relied on me quite a bit.]
Jin chuckled again at this.
"Hey, Lokia. Does thinking that way bring you some comfort?"

Even as Jin laughed, he continuously struck the outer armor of Kri. Kri kept becoming transparent, neutralizing Jin's sword, but now, unlike before, small fragments were flying off. The Red Plutonian's technology was gradually failing to keep up with Sigmund's speed.
"Besides Knight Sarah, who else were you close to? Butler Léat? Knight Frey? Maybe, you were really close to them. But what kind of expression do you think they would have seeing you now?"
In Jin's view, Lokia was an enemy with clear weaknesses.
She still hadn't moved on from her glorious clan of a thousand years ago.

"Sticky and filthy regrets, emotions you desperately deny, seem to cover even the murky winds of the battlefield. Disgusting. You've lost too much to move forward, and you know it better than anyone."
Fzzzt!

The blue blade sliced through the central part of Kri. The armor that failed to become transparent and the magic circuits filling it were torn apart. The parts fell stickily like flesh, oxidized by the lightning energy.
Slowly but surely.
Kri was being destroyed. Wherever Jin's gaze landed, sword energy spread, and the blue lightning energy whipped up, shaking the massive hull.
The reattached cannon of Kri, like the eyes of a beast, ceaselessly followed Jin. Lokia had just released the lightning energy that had infiltrated the cannon.
Normally, precise aiming would have been unnecessary. Its attack range was wide enough to make evasion impossible.
But now, Jin was rampaging inside the hull. It was not easy to extract the cannon again and aim at Lafrarosa.
Because Jin was now more aware of the cannon's position than at the start. While initially, he couldn't keep a close check due to searching for Lokia's location, now it was different.
Jin had not lost track of her position for a moment since Lokia and the cannon returned to the hull.

'I've been outplayed. I should have released the lightning energy that had infiltrated the cannon from the outside, even if it meant some damage to Kri. Jin has been planning to exclude the possibility of me and this air fortress falling from the start, coming up with such a strategy without any prior information.'
The main weapon of Kri was the cannon. It was also the reason Lokia came to the great desert today. She intended to use that weapon to turn the battle in her favor.

[As you say, I still love the Runcandel of that time. More precisely, it's a love-hate relationship. Sigh, maybe that's why my plans always go slightly awry? Being tied up, I unknowingly make wrong moves.]
Suddenly, Lokia reflected on the past.
After Runcandel's defeat a thousand years ago, Lokia wandered the world like a specter, observing the Garden of Swords from afar.
For a thousand years, Lokia had at least dozens of opportunities to end Runcandel if she had so wished.

‘Chiron, and then Luna and Jin... I had hoped for the birth of such children. It was that hope that kept me from destroying the Garden of Swords, even as I wandered through the swamp of a distorted world and manipulated history.’
Her heart swelled.
Lokia was thrilled watching Jin wield his sword. A foolish yet strong person, still believing that the world could be changed and protected solely by a fighting spirit, was representing Runcandel.

[If you watch from a distance like I do... Runcandel can be seen as unchanging and eternal. That's what captivated me. Temar, Chiron, Luna, and you. People who could shine brilliantly without the witch, capable of making the world more righteous, kept emerging.]
Old, worn-out emotions that she thought had completely disappeared were resurfacing.

[But, your use of the Plutonian's sword, not Runcandel’s, doesn't suit you beautifully. Do you know? They are each a fragment of the sun. Therefore, they have no interest in changing the world. Just war and conquest, that's all they care about. Their sword doesn't suit you.]
Right after those words, Jin suddenly felt as if dozens of invisible hands were weighing him down.
It was because of his heart of light.
The inner chaos within Lingling, contained within it, began to churn, attempting to dissolve the fusion of Battle God.
The bond was weakening. The storm of the Plutonian Domination Sword that had dyed the battlefield deep blue was rapidly diminishing.
[It's time to cut off that bond. I've become curious about your own sword, not one of the disasters born of the sun.]
Instantly, the blue energy vanished from the battlefield. The vast energy seemed to be a lie.
Jin's heart of light turned a dull black and grew cold. The lightning energy no longer pulsed within it, and Sigmund lost its radiance, returning to its original, faint, and pale appearance.
"Oh no! Jin's fusion with the Battle God is..."
"The Plutonian Domination Sword has gone out! Damn it, is Jin alright?"
From the position of Murakan and the Battle Kings, the interior of Kri was completely obscured. All they could see was chaos rising like poison where the blue storm had disappeared.
"If the fusion of Battle God is gone, even Jin facing the origin chaos like that is dangerous, Murakan. Go to Jin quickly! We'll somehow protect Lafrarosa!"
Murakan felt a chill this time. The moment he left, Lokia would surely strike Lafrarosa in earnest, but Jin was always his priority.
At that moment, about to spread his wings, Murakan and the Battle Kings heard Jin's voice.
Lokia, the Plutonian's sword will soon be my sword.
Everyone on the battlefield heard it. Even those who had just arrived at the edge of the great desert, summoned by Jin, heard his voice.
"Like Solderet is the God of Runcandel, Vahn is my Battle God. I am Runcandel, and thus Vahn is the Battle God of Runcandel. All of this is entirely, my sword."
Just as using spiritual energy through a contract with Solderet doesn't make it any less Jin's power, the fusion of Battle God is no less than Jin's sword.
"I've become too strong for you to handle."
Paaa...
Wherever the blue lightning energy had disappeared, wherever the chaos had sullied the battlefield in its place.
Brilliant golden lightning energy was bursting forth. A dazzling golden wind was rising.

"You said the Runcandel you watched from afar is unchanging and eternal. No, a clan is just a collection of people, and people are meant to change. But it shines because of something that we try not to forget, despite all the time and changes."
Lokia's spirit appeared behind Jin. The spirit, trying to stab Jin with a black blade, was engulfed by the golden lightning and vanished somewhere.

"Lokia, I hoped that you would make me understand once. Reasons why you had to betray the clan, why your ideal was necessary for this world... But now, you're no different from the madmen I've seen. Trying to ruin a world that's doing just fine, all you'll get is emptiness."

Lokia didn't respond. She had certainly infiltrated Lingling and the heart of light with chaos to break the fusion of Battle God. The flashing light now emanating from Jin was completely beyond her comprehension, despite a thousand years of exploring the secrets and truths of the world.
[...Jin, I never intended to kill the Battle God of Lafrarosa. She had his uses. But that was a mistake. I need to kill her, or she might truly become another Solderet or even the Sun God.]
The chaos dimension portal began to open in the sky. Lokia was sending out new spirit forms through it.
It was a risky move she hadn't anticipated. The Vamel Alliance had the only record magician, who could examine that dimension portal and trace the location of her real body. Her 'World of Lokia.'
That was the information Jin most wanted to gain from this battle.
"Now you're even worrying about trivial things."
Then, Jin raised his sword. It was time to unfold the final move of the Plutonian's Domination Sword Secret Technique.
